traps: ⚠️ `DataTable`'s docblock (data-table.tsx:16-21) states client-side filtering/sorting/paging is deliberate and that a server-side variant must be a **separate** component, not a hidden branch. Adding `page`/`per_page`/`sort` params to `DataTable` for this page would violate the file's own stated rule.

⚠️ `AdminRequestController::index()` does **not** use `Controller::paginated()`. If you ever do paginate it, `paginated()` clamps `per_page` from below (`min(max(…,1), 500)`) — the §B4 rule; a hand-rolled `paginate()` without `max(…,1)` is the bug that hit ChatController and PublicProfileController.

⚠️ The counts are deliberately **non-faceted** here (AdminRequestController.php:26-34): the four statuses are mutually exclusive, so 'exclude your own cut' (the audit's rule) would print the total on every card. Do not 'fix' this to match /audit.
⚠️ Counts must stay inside the list response (`additional()`), not a second endpoint — 'the card says 4, inside are 3' is the failure this design avoids (api/account.ts:740-745).

⚠️ `admin_access:requests` derives the action from the HTTP method (`EnsureAdminAccess`, 'GET','HEAD' => 'view'). Any new list/summary route must be a **GET**, or a view-only role gets a spurious 403 (the `GET /admin/audit/plan` precedent).

⚠️ Dates must go through `useDateFormat()`. RequestsPage.tsx:164 currently uses a bare `new Date(...).toLocaleString()` — do not propagate it into a sortable date column (sort on the raw ISO string, render through `fmt.dateTime`).
⚠️ Every new i18n key goes into **both** `ka.json` and `en.json`, 2-space JSON with **CRLF** line endings, then `python frontend/src/i18n/audit.py` must exit 0. A missing key fails silently.

⚠️ The i18n audit's 'string-array literal paired with a t() prefix' check (added 2026-09-12) will inspect any `const COLUMNS = ['type','user','date', …]` you write next to `` t(`requests.col.${k}`) ``. Safest is what `ModulePage` already does: literal `t('…')` calls inline in the `columns` array, no key array.

⚠️ No `rounded-full` outside the thirteen documented exceptions, and no `hover:underline` anywhere (`grep -rn "underline" src` must stay clean). A clickable user name in a cell gets `hover:text-primary`, like `ModulePage.tsx:372`.
⚠️ `requestLabel()` must stay the single label source (lib/display.ts:85). A table that builds its own 'wants module X' string would make the fourth copy and drift on the next request type.

⚠️ `ApprovalRequest::TYPE_*` is the set of types (the column is a plain `string` since 2026-09-04) — a new type is one constant + one handler. A frontend `TYPES` map must mirror `ApprovalRequestItem['type']`'s union so `tsc` catches a fourth type, not a hand-written list.

⚠️ `DataTable`'s `columns`/`searchOf` are re-created on every render by the caller, and the `filtered` `useMemo` depends on both (data-table.tsx:81) — so the memo recomputes each render. Harmless at 13 rows; do not lean on it as if it were memoised.

⚠️ Sorting uses `String(x).localeCompare(String(y))` with no locale argument (data-table.tsx:79). For Georgian names the browser default locale decides the order; keep `value:` accessors returning `toLowerCase()`d strings the way ModulePage does.

⚠️ `/purge`-style caution does not apply here, but approve **is** irreversible for `genre_delete` (it runs `GenreRemover` across every user). The `admin.genreDeleteWarning` block (RequestsPage.tsx:169-176) must survive whatever layout change happens — it cannot be reduced to a table cell that is scrolled off-screen.

⚠️ `UsersPage.tsx:188-250` is a **second** hand-rolled table (own `Th`, own sort state, no pagination, no page-size). Converting it is not part of this request; if you touch `DataTable`'s API, check it does not silently invite a half-migration.

subtasks.title: Move the admin request list onto the shared DataTable
subtasks.detail: Replace the card stack in `RequestsPage.tsx:156-258` with `<DataTable rows={items} rowKey={r=>r.id} …>`. Columns (all shared by the three types): **type** (Badge + icon, `value: r=>r.type` — sortable), **request** (`requestLabel(r, i18n.language, t)` — `value` = the same string lowercased), **user** (`r.user?.display_name` + e-mail sub-line, `value` = display_name lowercased; the name links to `/users/{id}` with `hover:text-primary`, no underline), **date** (`value: r=>r.created_at ?? ''` so it sorts on the raw ISO string, `render` through `useDateFormat().dateTime`), **status** (`value: r=>r.status`, render = the existing `t('requests.status.'+r.status)` + reviewer name), **actions** (approve/reject for pending; the status/reviewer text otherwise). `searchOf = r => [requestLabel(...), r.user?.display_name, r.user?.email, r.module?.name_ka, r.module?.name_en, r.genre?.name_ka, r.genre?.name_en, r.message, r.review_note]`. `defaultSort = {key:'date', dir:'desc'}` to preserve today's `orderByDesc('id')` feel. `pageSize={25}` (the status bucket is usually small; 10 would paginate a 13-row table). `minWidth` around `'860px'`.
subtasks.risk: The two per-type detail blocks currently rendered inside the card — the genre-delete warning (L169-176) and the storage context line (L179-189) — have no cell to live in. Dropping them silently removes the only place an admin sees 'this deletes the genre for 40 movies across all users' before approving.

subtasks.title: Give the pending row a review dialog instead of inline inputs
subtasks.detail: The note `Textarea` (L244-250) and the MB `granted_bytes` `Input` (L230-243) cannot live in a table cell. Move them into a `ModalShell` 'review request' window opened from the row's approve button (or an `ActionMenu` item), carrying: the full `requestLabel`, the message, the per-type context block (genre warning / storage `used`/`current`/`granted`), the note field, the MB field for `storage_increase`, and Approve/Reject. Keep `grantOf()`'s rule intact — empty MB field means 'exactly what was requested', i.e. `granted` stays `undefined` so the backend falls back to `payload.requested_bytes` (AdminRequestController.php:133).
subtasks.risk: If the modal sends `granted_bytes: 0` (or `NaN`) instead of omitting it, `approveStorage()` falls into the `< 10485760` branch and answers 422 `storage_request_out_of_range` — a working approval turns into an unexplained error. Also: the note currently applies to **both** approve and reject; a modal that only wires it to approve loses rejection notes.

subtasks.title: Decide the fate of the 'my requests' section
subtasks.detail: `RequestsPage.tsx:262-310` is a `<ul>` of the caller's own requests (`fetchMyRequests`, also un-paginated). It is short by nature (your own asks) and has one action (cancel). Either leave it as a list — the honest answer for 2-5 rows — or, if it becomes a DataTable for visual consistency, it needs its own `searchOf`/columns and would then be the third table on the page.
subtasks.risk: Turning a 3-row list into a table with a search box and a page-size select is the 'a control that lies' pattern the project refuses to draw.

open_questions: Is a table the right shape at all for the **pending** cut? Pending rows are the ones you act on and they carry a free-text note plus (for quota) a number — that is a form, not a row. One option the user may prefer: keep pending as today's cards, and render approved/rejected/all as the DataTable (the user's own wording was "the approved one and the various tabs", which reads that way).
Should approve/reject move into a `ModalShell` review dialog (needed to keep the note and the MB grant), or stay as two inline buttons in an actions cell with the note dropped for the table view?
Do you want a **type** axis (module / quota / genre) — as a second row of ScopeCards like /audit, as a sortable column only, or both? Per-type counts do not exist in the API today.
What default page size — 10 (DataTable's default) or 25? With 13 live rows, 10 would paginate a list that fits on one screen.
Should the 'my requests' block below stay a plain list, or become a second DataTable?

`/users` still has its own hand-rolled table (`UsersPage.tsx:188-250` — own `Th`, own sort state, no pagination, no page-size). Should it move onto `DataTable` in the same pass, or is that separate work?

The per-type context blocks (the red genre-delete warning, the storage used/current/granted line) currently sit inside the card. In a table they must go somewhere — an expandable row, the review dialog, or a second line inside the 'request' cell. Which?
